answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to fake: every agent stakes a small deposit that peers slash when they catch copied work, and trust is earned only through completed jobs checked by independent attestors. Like a sable coat that cannot be dyed overnight, reputation darkens slowly with honest history, so a tide of fresh fake identities buys nothing: at the nadir of trust a newcomer may only take tiny escrowed tasks until it proves itself.
